planting.note: Plant offsets in spring or fall by pressing them onto the surface of very well-drained, gravelly soil in full sun; Granat is exceptionally cold hardy and far more likely to be lost to winter wet than to frost.

directions: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun. Granat forms a tidy, symmetrical rosette of pointed leaves that hold a deep burgundy-red color through the entire growing season rather than flushing red only at the tips or in cold weather, making it one of the more uniformly dark-colored sempervivum cultivars. In late summer to early fall it sends up clusters of small pink star-shaped flowers on a short stalk, later in the season than the early-summer bloom typical of many hens and chicks. It offsets readily to form a spreading mat and is reliably hardy to roughly zone 3, tolerating hard winter cold far better than wet, poorly drained soil, which remains the main threat to the planting.

planting.note: Plant offsets or container stock in spring in well-drained, gritty soil in full sun to part shade; Blue Atoll grows quickly for a large-rosette echeveria and offsets freely, so allow room for the clump to spread.

directions: Plant in well-drained, gritty to sandy soil in full sun to part shade. Blue Atoll, a hybrid bred by Australian succulent breeder Mal Morgan, forms broad rosettes up to about 8 inches across of thick, softly powdered blue-green leaves that offset freely to build a wide clump faster than many comparably large-rosette echeverias. The farina coating gives the foliage a frosted, matte look that is easily marked by handling or overhead watering, so water at the soil line and avoid brushing the leaves. Like other echeveria it needs sharp drainage and infrequent, deep watering, letting the soil dry out fully between waterings, and should be moved under cover or into a greenhouse before hard freezes.

common_name: Jewel of Desert Ruby Ice Plant

planting.note: Set out rooted plugs in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; like other Jewel of Desert selections, winter wet rather than cold is the main threat to its survival.

directions: Plant rooted plugs in spring into lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun. Jewel of Desert Ruby bears two-inch, daisy-shaped flowers in a deep ruby-red that is richer and more saturated than the plain rose-pink of the species, held above a dense, tight mat of small succulent leaves that stays lower and more compact than older seed-grown Delosperma cooperi. It blooms continuously from spring until frost and is part of a series bred for cold hardiness to roughly zone 5 as well as a tidier habit, making it useful for rock gardens, retaining-wall tops, and hot, dry xeriscape plantings where sharp drainage can be assured.

common_name: Jewel of Desert Opal Ice Plant

planting.note: Set out rooted plugs in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; good winter drainage matters more to survival than cold air temperature.

directions: Plant rooted plugs in spring into lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun. Jewel of Desert Opal produces pale pink, two-inch, daisy-shaped flowers with a soft iridescent sheen and a bright yellow center, a gentler pastel tone than the more saturated reds and purples of other selections already in this series. It forms the same dense, low, evergreen mat typical of the Jewel of Desert line and flowers continuously from spring through fall. Reliably hardy to about zone 5 with sharp winter drainage, it suits rock gardens, gravel beds, and container plantings where a restrained, tidy grower is preferred over the more vigorous species form.

common_name: Jewel of Desert Moonstone Ice Plant

planting.note: Set out rooted plugs in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; this patented selection shares the series' intolerance of standing winter moisture.

directions: Plant rooted plugs in spring into lean, gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun. Jewel of Desert Moonstone is the white-flowered member of the series, covering its dense, dark-green succulent mat in two-inch, bright white daisy-like blooms with a small yellow eye from spring until frost, a clean contrast to the pinks, reds, and purples of its series-mates already in this dataset. It is patented for its compact, floriferous, everblooming habit and shares the same cold hardiness to roughly zone 5 and intolerance of winter wet common to the Jewel of Desert line. Use it in rock gardens, raised beds, or containers where its pale color can set off neighboring hot-colored succulents.
